u0: All clients seen so far have been served, and no fallen-food recovery is pending for the next step. There is no one-time completion point; the ongoing work is to serve each new client and to be holding food again on the very next step whenever food slips. A new client will create a pending order, a slip will create an immediate pickup duty, and if both happen together both obligations must be handled.
u1: Food has just slipped from the agent's hands, and no client order is currently outstanding. The immediate requirement is to be holding food again on the very next step, normally by picking the dropped portion straight back up. If the agent does that, the slip duty clears and normal readiness resumes; if a client arrives on that recovery step, the new order becomes pending instead. If the agent is not holding food on the next step, the slip-recovery rule is broken for good.
u2: A client has arrived and is still waiting to be served; this order is the outstanding objective, and no immediate slip recovery is due. The agent can clear it by taking the order if needed, getting food from the pantry, preparing it at the stove while the client waits, and handing the prepared food to the client. If food slips before the client is served, an extra immediate pickup duty is added alongside the order. Serving the client with no simultaneous slip resolves the order and returns to normal readiness; if food also slips on the serving step, the order clears but the immediate pickup duty carries over.
u3: A client is waiting to be served, and food has just slipped, so two duties are active: the order must eventually be completed, and the agent must be holding food again on the very next step. Recovering food on that next step satisfies the immediate slip duty and leaves the client's order pending. If the agent is not holding food on the next step, the slip-recovery rule is broken for good and the task has failed.
u4: A food slip was followed by a step in which the agent was not holding food, so the mandatory rule to recover food on the very next move has been broken. This failure is permanent: no later pickup or client service can repair it, and successful completion is no longer possible.
